title: Dedicated capacity: Autoscale Negotiator, reserve arbitration and isolation controls PRD
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: Introduce an "autoscale negotiator" subsystem and operator controls that allow short-term, auditable reallocation of reserved capacity across dedicated tenant pools for graceful burst handling while preserving isolation SLAs. Problem: tenants with reserved capacity currently either hit hard limits (causing request rejects) or require manual admin intervention to borrow unused headroom. Goal: enable predictable, controlled, auditable micro-bursts and short-term lease transfers to avoid hard outages while guaranteeing tenant SLOs and tenancy isolation constraints.
background_and_context: Redwood Dedicated customers demand predictable throughput. Today we over-provision or accept spiky rejects. There are existing features for reserved pools and soft-evict policies, but they lack a negotiated, auditable path to temporarily borrow capacity without manual ops or unsafe preemption. This PRD scopes a negotiation-first autoscaler that enforces isolation classes, per-tenant credit budgets, and operator rollback.
non_goals: 1) Full automated cross-tenant preemption without explicit opt-in. 2) Permanent resizing of tenant contracts (billing/commits are out of scope). 3) Replacing the long-term capacity planning flow.
user_stories: As an SRE for a large customer, I want my tenant to automatically borrow short-term capacity during traffic spikes so that requests are not rejected, while keeping my committed performance SLA intact.
As a Redwood operator, I want visibility into all negotiated leases and an ability to revoke or rollback a lease within a defined grace period.
As a product owner, I want the console to show per-tenant credit balances, current leases, and simulated outcomes before approving a lease for a customer.
As a Dev on the serving runtime team, I want well-defined APIs that request and confirm temporary capacity so we can coordinate warmups and avoid cold-start latency.
As a compliance reviewer, I want all lease actions to be logged with tenant IDs, operator IDs, timestamps and rationale for auditability.
functional_requirements: FR-1: Negotiator API - POST /negotiator/leases to request a lease. Request includes tenant_id, requested_gpus, duration_seconds, priority_hint, isolation_class.
FR-2: Eligibility check - Negotiator returns allowed or denied with deterministic reason codes (e.g., ISOLATION_VIOLATION, INSUFFICIENT_HEADROOM, OPT_IN_REQUIRED).
FR-3: Credit budget - Each tenant has a configurable burst credit ledger; successful leases deduct credits proportional to requested capacity * duration.
FR-4: Arbitration policy - When multiple concurrent leases compete, the negotiator applies isolation_class ordering, parity fairness, and remaining credits to decide winners.
FR-5: Audit log - All actions emit immutable audit entries to the dedicated audit log with operators, requestor, and decision tree snapshot.
FR-6: Fallback - If a requested lease would violate isolation policies, the system offers suggested alternatives (reduced GPUs, shorter duration, or queued prewarm).
FR-7: Operator override - Admins can create, extend, revoke leases via the console with an optional justification note; overrides are auditable and require 2FA for P0 revocations.
FR-8: Runtime handshake - Serving runtime must accept a lease token and schedule prewarm/kv-cache allocation accordingly; lease expiry triggers graceful reclaim path.
FR-9: Billing signals - Negotiate temporary usage metrics into billing pipeline as 'burst usage' distinct from committed minutes for later billing reconciliation.
FR-10: Compatibility - Negotiator must support current reserved-pool topology and be deployable behind feature flag for gradual rollout to clusters.
FR-11: Console UX - Lease request flow in the console with simulated warmup latency and estimated SLO impact preview before submission.
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR-1: Decision latency - Eligibility checks must respond within 200ms 99th percentile to avoid adding micro-latency to request paths.
NFR-2: Audit durability - Audit entries are stored with 99.999% durability and appear in the console within 30s of action.
NFR-3: Safety - Any automated lease must guarantee that priority tenants marked 'isolation-critical' cannot be reduced beyond contract floor.
NFR-4: Observability - Time series for leases (active_count, reclaims, extensions) must be emitted to central telemetry with 1min resolution.
NFR-5: Resource correctness - The negotiator must never commit more GPUs than cluster headroom; any conservative allocation failures must prefer denial over overcommit.
api_spec: POST /negotiator/leases {tenant_id, requested_units, duration_s, priority_hint, requestor, opt_in_token?} -> {lease_id, status, granted_units, expires_at, reason_code} ; GET /negotiator/tenants/{tenant_id}/credits -> {credits_remaining, history_cursor} ; POST /negotiator/admin/revoke {lease_id, reason}. All endpoints must accept an idempotency_key and emit audit_id in response.
console_changes: New 'Burst requests' panel under Dedicated -> Capacity: request wizard that simulates warm-up and SLO impact, shows credit cost, displays alternative suggestions, and provides a one-click 'request' button. Admin view includes active lease timeline, revoke button with justification modal, and export-able audit CSV.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: A tenant can successfully request and receive a lease for up to 30% additional units over committed capacity for durations <= 1 hour when sufficient headroom exists, without violating higher-isolation tenants' floors.
AC-2: Negotiator decision latency <= 200ms P99 in a test cluster with 500 tenants and synthetic competing requests.

AC-3: All lease lifecycle events (create/extend/revoke/expire) produce an audit record containing lease_id, actor, tenant_id, original_request_json, decision_reason, and timestamp that is queryable in the console within 30s.

AC-4: Serving runtime can accept a lease token and warm KV cache within prewarm_time_estimate and begins scheduling incoming requests against granted units within 90s of lease creation for 'fast-warm' profiles.
AC-5: Console simulation must surface an estimated SLO delta and show >=90% accuracy (measured vs actual in canary traffic) for short bursts in canary clusters.
AC-6: Operator override flow requires 2FA when revoking a lease granted for a production tenant and logs the justification string in audit.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Automated reallocation could cause SLA regressions for isolation-critical tenants. Mitigation: enforce hard floors, require opt-in for any tenant where contract prohibits borrowing, and limit automated leases to configurable percentage. Risk: Billing confusion. Mitigation: label all burst usage clearly and generate post-burst reports and billing reconciliation alerts.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged API and console disabled by default. 2) Internal canary with non-production tenants for 2 weeks. 3) Beta with 5 trusted customers with opt-in. 4) Gradual ramp to 25% clusters with telemetry validation (SLO delta under threshold). 5) General availability after security review and billing backfill completed.
change_log: 2025-02-12: Initial PRD created by Aisha Kapoor. 2025-02-20: Scope change - removed automatic cross-tenant preemption from automated path; replaced with 'negotiated lease' flow following legal and privacy review (reason: cross-tenant preemption raised contracts and compliance concerns). 2025-02-28: Added 2FA requirement for operator revokes at PM request.
notes: Next steps: align on SLO test harness with Runtime team (ENG-9102), finalize audit retention policy with Security, and draft billing reconciliation plan with Finance. Schedule a cross-functional kickoff the week of 2025-03-03.)
